title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Nova Financial
next_steps: Redwood to send completed SIG/CAIQ export and evidence links
Customer to confirm required data residency region and provide list of required evidences
Schedule follow-up call for evidence review week of 2025-09-22
action_items: Maya Lin - send SIG/CAIQ export + SOC2 report link by 2025-09-16
Jordan Patel - prepare short diagram of VPC/private deployment options by 2025-09-19
Priya Desai - list required evidence artifacts (log samples, key rotation policy) by 2025-09-18
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood's SIG/CAIQ responses and evidence mapping for Nova Financial. Discussed SOC 2 scope, ISO plans, RBAC/SSO integration, audit logs, encryption/KMS options, and data residency. Agreed next steps for evidence handoff and follow-up evidence review call.
topics: Data residency and private deploy options
transcript:
00:00 Maya Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood inference, I'm the AE on this account. Quick roll call?
00:08 Ethan Cole: Ethan, CISO, Nova Financial. Sorry running a bit late.
00:12 Priya Desai: Priya, security analyst, here.
00:15 Mark Liu: Mark, procurement.
00:17 Jordan Patel: Jordan, SE at Redwood.
00:20 Sara Gomez: Sara, legal. Good afternoon.
00:24 Maya Lin: Great, thanks. The objective for today is a SIG/CAIQ walkthrough and to map what evidence you need. We'll go section by section and call out where we can provide docs or artifacts.
00:35 Priya Desai: Sounds good. We're mostly concerned about SOC 2 coverage, encryption in transit and at rest, KMS, and data residency for regulated data.
00:44 Jordan Patel: Perfect — quick heads up, our SIG export covers the CAIQ categories. We'll also attach the SOC 2 Type II report and our controls matrix; some of the wording in the SIG is auto-mapped and may need slight clarification.
00:57 Ethan Cole: When you say "attach SOC 2 Type II" is that the full report or a redacted version? We will need evidence of control operation, not full client data.
01:05 Maya Lin: We can provide the full SOC 2 Type II under an NDA; usually customers get a redacted report plus a link to the auditor's letter. We'll include the auditor name and test dates.
01:14 Priya Desai: OK. On RBAC — how granular is it? Can we sync with our SSO and control role-to-group mapping?
01:23 Jordan Patel: Yes. We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. Roles are configurable; by default we have admin, developer, viewer and custom roles support. There is also API-key based service accounts with scoped permissions.
01:38 Priya Desai: Is there separation between environment-level admin and org-level admin? We need separation for prod vs dev.
01:45 Jordan Patel: Yep, you can scope roles at project/route/model level. There's a notion of org admin and project admin; we'll show a diagram in the follow up.
01:53 Mark Liu: On data residency — are you hosting EU data in eu-1 region only, or is it multi-region replication? We have GDPR requirements for some workloads.
02:03 Sofia Ramos: Our hosted offering supports region pinning; for EU data we can pin to eu-west-1. By default we don't replicate customer content outside the pinned region unless you opt in for cross-region failover. For strict residency customers we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) deployment or Dedicated in a committed region.
02:18 Priya Desai: And for private deployments, do you run a separate control plane or is it customer-managed?
02:24 Jordan Patel: Private deployments can be customer-managed; there are two flavors: VPC with Redwood-managed control plane but customer network controls, or fully on-prem where both control plane and runtime are in-customer environment.
02:36 Ethan Cole: For SOC 2 evidence, we'll need log samples for admin activity, user provisioning events, and key rotation records. Can you provide structured log exports?
02:45 Jordan Patel: Yes, audit logs are available via our logging API and can be exported to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/BigQuery). The logs include actor, action, target, timestamp, and request id. Note sometimes names in the export are service accounts not human names — there can be mapping.
03:00 Priya Desai: What's retention? We need 1 year of immutable logs with a WORM option.
03:06 Sofia Ramos: Default retention is 90 days, we offer extended retention as an add-on up to 7 years. For WORM/immutable storage we integrate with customer-controlled S3 buckets and lifecycle policies.
03:18 Sara Gomez: Do you have attestations for encryption at rest? KMS? HSM?
03:23 Jordan Patel: We use customer-managed KMS keys for Private deployments and Dedicated customers; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS and can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer KMS for primary key wrapping. We don't hold plaintext keys. For HSM-level attestations we can provide details of KMS provider and configuration, and we can supply key rotation policies and logs as evidence.
03:47 Ethan Cole: How do you manage secrets inside the runtime — are they stored encrypted and rotated?
03:52 Jordan Patel: Secrets are stored encrypted at rest using AES-256 and the key material is protected by KMS. Rotation is supported; we can provide the rotation schedule and proof-of-rotation logs.
04:05 Priya Desai: Regarding network segmentation, can we use our own VPC endpoints and restrict egress?
04:10 Sofia Ramos: Yes, for VPC/private we provision ENIs and private endpoints; egress can be restricted and you control peering and NAT. We'll include the network diagram in the artifact bundle.
04:22 Mark Liu: For the SIG, are the responses prepopulated or do you manually edit them? We've seen mismatches in auto-exported answers before.
04:30 Maya Lin: The SIG export is auto-generated from our security questionnaire repo, then reviewed by our security team. We usually hand-edit answers flagged as "customer specific". We'll mark items where evidence is required.
04:42 Priya Desai: Can you walk through a couple of SIG control items related to key lifecycle and access reviews?
04:48 Jordan Patel: Sure — Q: Key lifecycle management (CAIQ section cryptography). Our concise answer: keys are centrally managed, rotation enforced every 90 days for KEK, and access to key material limited to a small ops group with MFA and just-in-time elevation. Evidence: key rotation logs, access review logs, and control owner contact. We'll attach rotation logs as redacted csv and the policy doc.
05:12 Ethan Cole: For access reviews, do you have a defined cadence and evidence of past reviews?
05:18 Jordan Patel: We perform quarterly access reviews; evidence is PDF exports of review meetings and the change tickets in Jira. We'll provide a sample from the last quarter.
05:27 Priya Desai: On vulnerability management, do you run internal scans and third-party pen tests?
05:31 Jordan Patel: We have weekly internal scanning, and annual pen tests by a third party. We provide summary reports, remediation tickets, and timelines. Full pentest reports sometimes need an NDA.
05:43 Priya Desai: Ok please note we will need a copy of the last pen test and the SOC 2 bridge if available.
05:49 Maya Lin: Noted — we'll include those.
05:51 Sara Gomez: A few legal asks — retention of personal data, deletion process, and subprocessor list.
05:57 Maya Lin: We'll send the DPA, subprocessors list, and deletion workflow.
06:02 Ethan Cole: About logging detail — sample log line please — does it include request/response bodies?
06:08 Jordan Patel: We do not include full response bodies in audit logs. We log request metadata, timestamps, user id, request id, response status and token usage metrics. For customers who require redaction we can mask sensitive fields and set logging level.
06:23 Priya Desai: For model caching or KV cache, is there any residual customer data persisted beyond TTL? We need to ensure no customer PII is cached or retained beyond policy.
06:33 Sofia Ramos: Our KV cache stores model state and can be configured to not persist prompts, or to purge prompt text after generation. For regulated workloads we recommend disabling prefix caching and using per-request ephemeral KV. We'll document configuration options.
06:50 Mark Liu: On SLA and incident mgmt — do you provide incident reports with root cause?
06:55 Jordan Patel: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we provide post-incident reports with timeline, RCA and mitigation. Hosted customers get incident summaries and can opt into faster notifications with PagerDuty hooks.
07:07 Priya Desai: A question on encryption in transit — TLS versions and cipher suites?
07:12 Jordan Patel: We enforce TLS 1.2+ and recommend 1.3 where supported. Cipher suites are industry standard — we'll include the full list in the evidence zip.
07:20 Ethan Cole: For the evidence exchange — what's the channel? Do you put artifacts in a secure bucket or use an encrypted share?
07:27 Maya Lin: We typically provision a secure, time-limited S3 share or use an encrypted Box folder. For the SOC 2 and pen-test we'll put them behind an NDA link. We'll also post machine-readable SIG/CAIQ export in JSON and a CSV mapping.
07:40 Priya Desai: We also have specific vendor form questions regarding data residency and subprocessors. Can you confirm subprocessors and any downstream AI model providers?
07:49 Jordan Patel: Subprocessors include cloud providers (AWS/GCP), KMS provider, monitoring vendor, and telemetry providers. For model artifacts we use open models and occasionally community model hosting; we don't send customer content to third-party model hosts without explicit agreement.
08:02 Priya Desai: Please ensure we get the subprocessors list. Also need confirmation that output from models is not used to train downstream models.
08:10 Maya Lin: Affirmative — by default we do not use customer content to train models. We'll include that statement and the policy doc.
08:17 Sara Gomez: If we move to Dedicated or Private later, how much re-onboarding is required for compliance?
08:24 Jordan Patel: Minimal — it's largely infra configuration and tenancy changes. The control evidence remains the same but deployment-specific artifacts will be added. We'll summarize differences in a short doc.
08:36 Mark Liu: Timeline wise we need to close vendor risk by 2025-10-01. Is that feasible?
08:41 Maya Lin: Yes, assuming we can get the evidence list to you by 2025-09-16 and your team reviews within a week we can meet that date.
08:49 Priya Desai: One last technical — key rotation proofs, can you provide KMS audit logs showing rotate events?
08:54 Jordan Patel: Yes, for customers on BYOK or Dedicated we can provide rotation event logs. For hosted we can provide high-level rotation attestations; if you need low level events we recommend Dedicated or BYOK.
09:07 Ethan Cole: OK let's recap next steps.
09:10 Maya Lin: I'll send the SIG export, SOC 2 Type II link, pen test statement, subprocessors list and the DPA by EOD tomorrow 2025-09-16. Jordan will add the network and VPC diagrams and key lifecycle docs. Priya to share the exact evidence checklist and any redlines to the SIG answers. We'll set a follow up for week of 2025-09-22 to review provided artifacts.
09:32 Priya Desai: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
09:35 Maya Lin: Thanks, we'll follow up with the link.
09:37 Meeting end
